headline: Jet-fuel prices to stay elevated well into 2027 unless Middle East conflict resolves
dek: Ryanair says profits dropped over rising fuel costs and that 'unless there is a swift resolution of the Middle East conflict, we expect jet-fuel prices to remain elevated well into 2027,' per CEO Michael O'Leary. No profit figure or fuel-price number was published in the liveblog entry in-window.
sources: Ryanair CEO Michael O'Leary, via Al Jazeera liveblog
fault_line: Who pays for Hormuz: the airlines say passengers will, deep into 2027 -- or does a 48-hour reopening deal erase that bill?

sections.what_happened: Ryanair says profits dropped over rising fuel costs and that 'unless there is a swift resolution of the Middle East conflict, we expect jet-fuel prices to remain elevated well into 2027,' per CEO Michael O'Leary. sections.what_verified: Single liveblog entry carrying the CEO statement
sections.what_disputed: None in-window; note this is one airline's earnings framing, not a market-wide fuel-price measurement -- Brent fell ~3% Monday on Doha-talk hopes (1000-02), so the 'elevated' claim is about levels vs pre-war, not Monday's direction.
sections.why_matters: Supporting pocketbook beat for the Hormuz lead: even if the strait reopens in 48 hours, Ryanair says your ticket already carries the war into 2027.
